background: An image-song about time passing over one night of love. A young man asks the new moon to shine bright tonight so he can go to white Jane. On the way there the cherries are in blossom, the wheat is in the ear and the springs are running; on the way back everything is picked, harvested and dried up.
background_source: Source of these notes: Qwen's draft.
en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Dialect verb forms (ц'теја, класеја, обрале, ожнале) translated by my reading: the trip there happens in spring bloom, the return finds everything harvested and the water dry (time passing).

lines.en: Oh Moon, new moon, oh dear,
Shine brightly this evening, oh dear,

lines.cyr: по бела Јана, леле, ќ' одиме.
lines.lat: po bela Jana, lele, ḱ' odime.
lines.en: we are going to white Jana, oh dear.
When we went to Jana, oh dear,
sour cherries and cherries, oh dear, were blooming.
Sour cherries and cherries were blooming, oh dear,
white wheat, oh dear, was in ear.
White wheat was in ear, oh dear,

lines.cyr: и в' зори вода, мори, течеја.
lines.lat: i v' zori voda, mori, tečeja.
lines.en: and at dawn water, hey, was flowing.
When we were coming back, oh dear,
sour cherries and cherries, oh dear, had been picked.
Sour cherries and cherries had been picked, oh dear,
white wheat, oh dear, had been reaped.
White wheat had been reaped, oh dear,

lines.cyr: и в' зори вода, леле, секнале.
lines.lat: i v' zori voda, lele, seknale.
lines.en: and at dawn the water, oh dear, had dried up.
